questions.question: When did the Government of India bring the gender sensitivities of the budgetary allocation in its statement for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**2005 - 06.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India brought** gender sensitivities of budgetary allocation** in its statement for the first time in **2005-06.**
 
• This reflects the government's recognition of the importance of gender in budgetary allocation and the need to address** gender inequalities** in the allocation of resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gender budgeting aims to improve **women's access** to public resources and mainstream their concerns in all activities by keeping an eye on spending and public service delivery from a gender viewpoint.
 
• The increased knowledge of **gender sensitivity** has given rise to this phrase.
 
• The **gender budget allocation** for **2019–20 **will be increased from **Rs 121,961 crore to Rs 131,700 crore **per the Finance Minister's proposal.
 
• The Minister advocated for women-led development to become the government's catchphrase in place of** "women's development,"** emphasizing programs for women's** employment, nutrition, and anganwadi.**

questions.question: Which of these measures of money supply is referred to as the aggregate monetary resources?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M3.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M3** is the measure of money supply that includes all the components of **M2 (currency, demand deposits, and time deposits)** as well as large-time **deposits,** repurchase **agreements,** and institutional **money market funds.**
 
• **M3** is often referred to as the **aggregate monetary resource** because it represents the broadest measure of money supply.
 
• **M4** is another measure of money supply that includes all the components of M3 as well as holdings of **money market instruments,** such as commercial paper and treasury bills.
 
• **MI, or monetary base**, is the narrowest measure of money supply and includes only currency in circulation and reserves held by **banks **at the central bank.
 
• **M2** is a broader measure of money supply than** MI.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **M4** is **not** as commonly used as the other measures of money supply.
 
• **MI **is often used as a tool for **monetary policy,** as changes in the monetary base can affect the amount of lending and borrowing in the economy.
 
• **M2** is often used as an** indicator of economic activity**, as the level of deposits in the economy can indicate the level of consumer and business spending.
 
• **M3** is often used as an indicator of **inflationary pressures,** as an increase in the money supply can lead to an increase in prices.

questions.question: _____________ is/are an item for which both, GST and central excise duty are applicable in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tobacco and tobacco products.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• On** Tobacco and tobacco products, GST and central excise duty** are applicable in India.
 
• **GST **(Goods and Services Tax) is a consumption tax that is levied on the **sale of goods and services** in India.
 
• **Central excise duty** is a tax on the **production or manufacture** of goods in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GST** is a digital version of** VAT** that allows you to track products and services.

 
 
• The tax slabs for GST and VAT are the **same.**
 
 
 
• A** shop or an intermediary collects** central excise duty from a client as an indirect type of taxation.
 
 
• When the products are moved from the **production line to a warehouse,** they get paid.
 
• The **Central Excise Tariff Act of 1985** and the **Central Excise Act of 1944** both oversee this specific tax.
 
 
 
• Even though liquor hasn’t been brought under the purview of Goods and Services Tax, it still falls under other taxes that contribute to its rising prices. These taxes are:
 
 
• **Excise Duty**
 
• **VAT (Value Added Tax)**
 
 
 
• **Petroleum products**, on the other hand, are subject to GST and a different type of excise duty called the** Central Excise Duty** and **Additional Excise Duty**, but not the central excise duty mentioned in the question.
 
• All agricultural commodities are **exempt from GST,** but some of them may be subject to other taxes or duties depending on their nature and usage.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Governor General of India when the Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal for revenue collection by the East India Company?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Cornwallis.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** was the **Governor General of India** when the Permanent Settlement was introduced in **Bengal **for revenue collection by the East India Company.
 
• It was introduced in** 1793.**
 
• The Permanent Settlement was an agreement between the** East India Company** and the** zamindars **(landlords) of Bengal, under which the zamindars were given the** right to collect revenue** from the peasants in return for a fixed annual payment to the Company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Wellesley** was the **Governor General of India** from **1798 to 1805.**

 
 
• He is known for his policy of **Subsidiary Alliance,** which aimed to establish **British supremacy** in India by making Indian rulers dependent on the Company for military protection.
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie** was the **Governor General of India** from **1848 to 1856.**
 
 
• He is known for his policy of **Doctrine of Lapse,** which aimed to annex Indian states if they did not have a natural heir.
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning **was the Governor General of India during the Indian Rebellion of **1857.**
 
 
• He is known for his efforts to **suppress the rebellion** and for his subsequent policy of** liberalization and reform.**

questions.question: The length of the playing surface for Table Tennis is _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.74 m.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **playing surface **for Table Tennis is a rectangular shape with a length of** 2.74 m** and a width of **1.525 m.**
 
• The playing surface, or table, is** matte** and consistently dark in **color.**
 
• A net that is **15.25 cm tall **divides the table into two halves.
 
• Only** hardwood tables** or their derivatives are approved by the ITTF. 
 
• It is important to note that the playing surface for Table Tennis is also commonly referred to as the** Table Tennis table **or simply the Table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Table tennis** is a **racquet sport **that originated from tennis, although it differs from the game in that participants play on a **stationary table **rather than a court. 
 
• Players work in teams of two or individually, taking turns using **small rackets** to return a light, hollow ball over the** table's net** and onto the other half of the court.
 
• If they are **unable** to do so, the other team scores a point.
 
• With event categories for **men's and women's singles** as well as men's and women's teams since doubles were replaced in **2008**, table tennis has been an** Olympic sport** since **1988.**
 
• The **International Table Tennis Federation** (ITTF), established in** 1926,** is in charge of overseeing table tennis.
 
• There are presently **226 member associations** in the ITTF globally.

questions.question: Which of the following universities was founded by the Pala rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikramasila.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vikramasila University** was founded by the **Pala dynasty rulers** in the **8th century CE**, in present-day Bihar, India.
 
• The university was a major center for **Buddhist studies,** attracting scholars from all over India and other countries like** Tibet, China, and Korea.**
 
• The university had several faculties, including **philosophy, logic, grammar, and medicine**, and its curriculum emphasized both theoretical and practical aspects of learning.
 
• Vikramasila University declined in the **12th century** CE due to invasions by **Turkish armies** and a shift in patronage towards other centers of learning like **Nalanda and Odantapuri.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nalanda University** is located in present-day **Bihar, India.**

 
 
• It was founded in the **5th century CE **and became a renowned center for **Buddhist studies** and other disciplines like **astronomy, mathematics, and logic.**
 
• It had a vast campus, with several** temples, libraries, and lecture halls**, and attracted scholars and students from all over Asia.
 
• The university was destroyed by **Turkish invaders** in the **12th century **CE, and its ruins were rediscovered in the** 19th century** CE.
 
 
 
• **Valabhi University **is located in present-day **Gujarat, **India.
 
 
• It was founded in the **6th century CE **and became a major center for** Jain studies** and other disciplines like grammar, medicine, and astronomy.
 
• It had a well-organized curriculum and a **large library **and attracted students from all over India and other countries like** Sri Lanka and China.**
 
• The university declined in the** 8th century CE **due to political instability and invasions by Arab armies.
 
 
 
• **Taxila University** is located in present-day **Pakistan.**
 
 
• It was founded in the** 5th century BCE** and became a renowned center for **Buddhist and Hindu **studies, as well as other disciplines like medicine, astronomy, and philosophy.
 
• It had several faculties and a diverse student population, including** Greeks, Persians, and Chinese.**
 
• The university declined in the **5th century CE **due to political turmoil and invasions by Huns and other nomadic tribes.

questions.question: What is the aim of fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To establish political democracy.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The aim of **fundamental rights** mentioned in the Indian Constitution is to establish **political democracy. **
 
• Fundamental rights are the** basic rights **that every citizen of India is entitled to.
 
• These rights are essential for the development of a **democratic society.**
 
• The fundamental rights are enshrined in the Constitution to ensure that the citizens have the freedom to** express their views, form associations, and participate in the governance** of the country.
 
• The aim of fundamental rights is to establish political democracy by ensuring that every citizen has the** right to vote,** and the right to participate in the** decision-making process** of the government.
 
• The fundamental rights also ensure that the citizens have the **right to life, liberty, and equality before the law**, which are essential for the functioning of a democratic society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To establish a welfare state:**

 
 
• While the aim of fundamental rights is to establish a welfare state, it is** not **the primary aim.
 
• The primary aim is to establish **political democracy.**
 
 
 
• **To have absolute independence:**
 
 
• This option is not correct as the aim of fundamental rights is** not **to promote absolute independence but to ensure that citizens have the freedom to express their **views and participate** in the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **To promote economic justice:**
 
 
• While economic justice is an important aspect of fundamental rights, it is **not** the primary aim.
 
• The primary aim is to establish **political democracy.**

questions.question: What is the type of soil composed of silt and dust?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Loess.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Loess** is a type of soil composed of **silt and dust **that is formed from **wind-blown deposits.**
 
• It is typically found in areas with a** dry climate **and **sparse vegetation.**
 
• Loess is known for its high fertility, making it a **desirable soil** for agriculture.
 
• This type of soil is also **prone to erosion**, which can lead to problems like landslides and dust storms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Loam** is a type of soil that is a mixture of **sand, silt, and clay**.

 
 
• It is considered ideal for** plant growth.**
 
 
 
• **Marl **is a type of soil that is composed of **clay and calcium carbonate.**
 
 
• It is often used in** agriculture** to improve **soil quality.**
 
 
 
• **Podsol** is a type of soil that is found in **cold, moist climates.**
 
 
• It is characterized by a **thin layer of organic matter** and a layer of **iron and aluminum **compounds.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To develop the spirit of inquiry
To develop the spirit of harmony

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To bring reform.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• "To bring reform" is **not** a fundamental duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **"To develop humanism" **is a fundamental duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **"To develop the spirit of inquiry"** is a fundamental duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **"To develop the spirit of harmony"** is a fundamental duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental duties** are the moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a** spirit of patriotism** and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• Fundamental Duties were recommended by the **Swaran Singh Committee** in** 1976**, and their importance became apparent during the **internal emergency** of **1975–1977. **
 
• The fundamental duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the **42ⁿd Amendment Act in 1976.**
 
• Both people and the country are subject to the obligations outlined in **Part IV–A of the Constitution.**
 
• There are** 11 fundamental duties** mentioned in the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Sociologist Jan Breman described the change in the nature of the relationship between landlords, belonging to the dominant class, and agricultural workers, belonging to the low caste, as a shift from ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**patronage to exploitation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The shift from **patronage to exploitation** refers to a change in the relationship between** landlords and agricultural workers,** where landlords used to provide **support and protection** to workers but now exploit them for their labor.
 
• The rise in migrant agricultural labor was a result of the commercialization of agriculture.
 
• A **pattern of seasonal migration** developed, with thousands of workers moving between their **homes and more prosperous areas** where there is a demand for **labor and higher wages,** as traditional bonds between** laborers or tenants **and landlords broke down and as seasonal demand for agricultural laborers increased in prosperous areas.
 
• Workers also** leave rural areas** due to rising **inequality **that began in the mid-1990s and pushed many households to work several jobs in order to make ends meet.
 
• This change is significant because it reflects a shift in **power dynamics** between the **dominant class** and** low castes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tenant to tiller** does** not** reflect a change in the nature of the relationship between landlords and workers, but rather a change in the type of** labor arrangement.**

 
 
• Farmers, or land tillers, have the legal right to acquire** land ownership** under the "Land to Tiller" law.​
 
 
 
• **Exploitation to patronage** contradicts the description provided by Jan Breman and** does not** reflect a shift in power dynamics.
 
• **Bonded labor to free labor** refers to a specific type of l**abor arrangement **rather than a change in the nature of the relationship between landlords and workers.

questions.question: Jayalakshmi Eshwar won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2021 for her contribution to which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Bharatanatyam.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jayalakshmi Eshwar **has won the** Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2021** for her contribution to **Bharatanatyam**, an Indian classical dance form that originated in the southern state of **Tamil Nadu.**
 
• Bharatanatyam is known for its **intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and graceful movements.**
 
• It is usually performed by female dancers and often depicts stories from** Hindu mythology**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathakali **is a classical dance form from the southern state of **Kerala** that is known for its elaborate makeup, costumes, and facial expressions.

 
 
• It often depicts stories from the** Hindu epics** of **Ramayana and Mahabharata.**
 
• **Other artists: **Kalamandalam Gopi, Kottakkal Sivaraman, Kalamandalam Ramankutty Nair.
 
 
 
• **Kathak** is a North Indian classical dance form that combines **storytelling, footwork, and facial expression**s to convey emotions and moods.
 
 
• It is often performed by both **male and female** dancers.
 
• Other artists: Birju Maharaj, Pandit Durga Lal, Shovana Narayan.
 
 
 
• **Odissi** is a classical dance form from the eastern state of Odisha that is known for its **fluid movements, intricate footwork, and graceful gestures**.
 
 
• It often depicts stories from **Hindu mythology **and is usually performed by **female dancers.**
 
• Other artists: Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sanjukta Panigrahi, Ileana Citaristi.

questions.question: Which state in India had the lowest sex ratio according to the 2011 census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **2011 census, Haryana** had the **lowest sex ratio** among all states in India.
 
• The sex ratio in** Haryana** was **879 females **per **1000 males**, which was much lower than the national average of **943 females **per **1000 males.**
 
• This low sex ratio in Haryana can be attributed to various factors such as** female infanticide, gender-based discrimination**, and a preference for **male children.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Punjab **had a **sex ratio **of** 895 females per 1000 males **in the 2011 census, which was higher than Haryana but still lower than the national average.
 
• **Rajasthan** had a sex ratio of **926 females per 1000 males** in the 2011 census, which was higher than both Haryana and Punjab but still lower than the national average.
 
• **Bihar **had a sex ratio of **918 females per 1000 males** in the 2011 census, which was lower than both Punjab and Rajasthan but higher than Haryana.
 
• The proportion of women to men in a population is known as the **sex ratio.**
 
• In **2023,** there will be** 1,020 girls for every 1,000 males** in India.
 
• In rural areas, there are **949 females for every 1,000 men, **while in urban areas, there are **929 females for every 1,000** males.

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Indian Association, established in 1876?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surendranath Banerjee.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Surendranath Banerjee** was one of the founders of the** Indian Association**, established in **1876.**
 
• The **Indian Association** was a political organization formed to represent the interests of the **Indian community** and to promote political and social reforms in India.
 
• He was one of the founding members of the **Indian National Congress.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji **was a prominent Indian nationalist leader who was associated with the **Indian National Congress.**

 
 
• He is known as the** "Grand Old Man of India."**
 
 
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade **was a **social reformer** and a founder of the** Indian National Congress.**
 
 
• He worked for the **upliftment of women **and the** lower castes** in India.
 
 
 
• **Sisir Kumar Ghosh** was a** journalist** and a **political leader.**
 
 
• He founded the Bengali-language newspaper **"Amrita Bazar Patrika."**
